Modeling Approach: No optimisation model is built, the method works directly on the routing graph
Workflow: Negotiated congestion routing (PathFinder style rip up and reroute) builds a feasible packing: each net is routed as a greedy Steiner tree by multi source Dijkstra on node costs that grow with present and historical overuse, until no node is shared. Every net is then replaced in turn by a minimum Steiner tree of the grid with the other nets' nodes removed (Dreyfus Wagner recursion driven by Dijkstra, exact since nets have at most six terminals), repeated until no net improves. A large neighbourhood search then rips up two to four adjacent nets and re-inserts them exactly in every order, with small random node costs on the earlier nets and occasional random kicks, for a fixed time budget. The best packing seen is kept. No published solution is used at any point.
Hardware Specifications: Apple M3 Pro laptop (11 cores: 5 performance, 6 efficiency), 18 GB memory, macOS 26.3, Python 3.11.7, no GPU. Five single threaded runs at a time and nothing else running, on AC power.
Remarks: This instance has no entry in the best known table. 5 independent runs from scratch, seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, with 600 s of neighbourhood search after routing and exact polish.
